caption:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says Trump and Xi agreed that humans must always be involved in military decisions made with AI.
He told CNBC that AI should not be allowed to act on its own in major military actions.
The AI race goes on: Nvidia's H200 stays the most advanced chip China can buy.

Should AI ever be allowed to make war decisions on its own?

threads_text: Bessent says Trump and Xi agreed that no major military operation should launch without a human involved, even if AI is doing the thinking. Good news, but it is a verbal deal while the chip race keeps going. Do you trust a handshake on military AI?

site_article.seo_title: Trump and Xi agree humans must control military AI, Bessent says
site_article.seo_description: Scott Bessent says Trump and Xi agreed in Shenzhen that humans must always be involved in military AI decisions, while Nvidia H200 chip limits on China stay.
site_article.answer_summary: According to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Trump and Xi agreed that AI should not act autonomously in major military actions and that a human must always be involved.
site_article.hero_alt: Two leaders at a bilateral meeting during the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China.

paragraphs.text: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday, November 20, 2026, that President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed that humans should always be involved in military decisions that use artificial intelligence. Bessent made the comments in an interview with CNBC after returning from the leaders' meeting in Shenzhen, China, according to Reuters.

Trump and Xi held a bilateral meeting on November 19 at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen. Reuters reported that Bessent described the AI agreement as one of the major achievements of Trump's trip to Asia.
What Bessent said about AI and the military

According to Reuters, Bessent said the two leaders agreed that AI should not be allowed to act autonomously in major military actions, and that no major military operation should be launched without a human being involved. He used the term "SI," which Reuters described as the administration's term for super intelligence.

Anadolu Agency reported the same remarks and said Bessent also described a robust discussion on trade policy and AI during the trip. Neither report described a signed document or a formal text for the AI commitment, and the details of how it would be applied or checked were not given.

Bessent said the agreement would not be affected by the competition between the United States and China for AI supremacy. He argued that American AI labs must keep their lead, calling that lead the best defense against what he described as dangerous Chinese AI models used in cyberattacks, Reuters reported.

On chips, Bessent said Nvidia's H200 remained the most advanced chip China could buy with export licenses, after Trump took what Bessent called a very firm line. He pointed to a lack of Chinese orders for the H200 and said China was probably many years behind, according to Reuters.

Bessent also played down reported differences with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over AI chip restrictions, saying officials were committed to following Trump's instructions. Reuters noted that the Commerce Department took steps on Monday, November 16, to further restrict China's access to advanced AI chips, including remote access through data centers overseas.

Reuters also reported that Bessent called the trade talks robust without giving specifics, and that finalizing proposed tariff cuts falls to a fourth Trump and Xi meeting planned for mid-December at the G20 leaders summit in Miami.

Keeping a human in charge of decisions to use force is one of the most widely discussed principles in debates over military AI, and a public statement from the leaders of the two largest AI powers gives it new political weight. Based on the remarks reported so far, the commitment is a shared principle described by a US official rather than a detailed treaty, and it sits alongside an open race between the two countries over chips and models.
Watch whether Beijing confirms the AI commitment in its own words, and whether a written version emerges around the planned Trump and Xi meeting at the G20 summit in Miami in December.
